issues.body: NotifyState::authorize_topic_read constructs WacAuthorizer directly and treats WAC Allow as final. In contrast, LdpState::authorize_read subsequently calls compose_odrl_read when odrl-authz is enabled, applying deny-overrides and permit-extends. Thus a requester with WAC Read but an ODRL Deny cannot GET the topic yet can still subscribe, receive a token, and pass the receive re-check. This contradicts the diff's repeated claim that notifications use the same effective authorization as GET. The new tests instantiate only WAC state, so they cannot detect the bypass.
issues.fix_hint: Route notification Read checks through a shared LdpState helper that computes the same effective WAC+ODRL decision as GET without reading protected bytes. Add feature-on tests proving WAC Allow + ODRL Deny returns 403 before token minting/subscriber registration, and proving the intended permit-extends behavior (or explicitly and consistently narrow the public claims if notifications intentionally remain WAC-only).
issues.title: Notification authorization still bypasses the effective ODRL read policy

verdict.summary: Round 4 is stagnant: the round-3 major authorization mismatch remains. The new notification helper still invokes WacAuthorizer directly, while the actual LDP GET path additionally composes the optional ODRL gate with deny-overrides and permit-extends. Consequently, with odrl-authz enabled, WAC Allow plus ODRL Deny permits subscription/token minting and receive registration even though GET is forbidden. The added tests exercise only WAC and do not cover either feature-on composition direction.
